missed.claim: Besides roles, each object carries readability (OPEN/PRIVATE/INHERITED/APPLICATION/SYSTEM) and writability, enforced in the ORM row-access policy on top of the role. A role grant cannot read a SYSTEM-readable object or write a SYSTEM/APPLICATION-writable one, and PRIVATE records need a record share.

runAgent loads tools lazily with {unionOf:[agentRole]} and no requireExplicitObjectGrants, with categories DATABASE_CRUD, ACTION, DASHBOARD and WORKFLOW. Unlike the workflow AI step, a runAgent agent therefore gets tools for every object its role reaches by default, including OPEN system objects.

At query time, row-level predicates are resolved from the roles of the auth context (user, API key or application), not from the rolePermissionConfig. In agent runs, the agent role's RLS predicates are not the ones applied.
AI CRUD tools (chat, MCP, agents) are never generated for objects with readability SYSTEM, for inactive objects, or for workflow-related objects, whatever the role grants.
